note: An intermediate guitar week at 30 minutes a day: joining pentatonic boxes is the key skill and returns on five days in new forms (box 2, box 3, a new key, bends across the join, from memory), with legato and picking warm-ups, sus and add9 rhythm parts, chord tones and a melody up the neck.

plan.title: Week 1: off box 1
plan.summary: Join the A minor pentatonic boxes 1 to 3, bend and slide across the joins, and use sus chords, chord tones and a melody to keep it musical.

exercises.title: Hammer and pull
exercises.focus: Legato trill · fingers 1-3 · G string, 5th fret

sections.text: Hammer-ons and pull-offs let notes flow without picking, and they build the strength the joins need.
Pick the first note only, then hammer finger 3 and pull back to finger 1, evenly on the click, for 30 seconds. Rest, then again at 80. Done when both notes are as loud as each other.

exercises.title: D, Dsus2, Dsus4
exercises.focus: Sus colours on D · strummed at 80 bpm

sections.text: Sus chords move one finger off and back on, which turns a plain chord into a moving part.
The three shapes
From D, lift your finger off the high E string for Dsus2, then add your pinky on its 3rd fret for Dsus4. Strum each, and switch D to Dsus4 to D to Dsus2 slowly, ten times.
As a groove
Press Play and strum along, one bar each: D, Dsus4, D, Dsus2. Keep the strumming hand moving and change only the one finger.

exercises.title: Box 1 to box 2
exercises.focus: A minor pentatonic · boxes 1 → 2 · 70 then 80 bpm

sections.text: One slide on the G string is all it takes to leave box 1 behind.
Box 2 on its own
Box 2 up and down at 70, one note per click. Its {{1}} notes are on the D and B strings.
Cross on the G string
Climb box 1; on the G string slide {{4}} (D, 7th fret) up to {{5}} (E, 9th fret) and finish in box 2. Come back the same way. Four clean runs.
At 80
The same crossing at 80 with the click. Done when the slide lands in time twice in a row.

exercises.title: Improvise across the join
exercises.focus: Boxes 1-2 over Am7-Dm7

sections.text: Using the join in a solo is what makes it stick.
Land on the roots
Press Play and improvise in boxes 1 and 2, crossing once per phrase. Land on {{a}} over Am7 and on {{d}} over Dm7.
Start in box 2
Same backing; now start every phrase in box 2 and end it in box 1.

exercises.title: Alternate picking
exercises.focus: Down-up, four notes per string, 90 bpm

sections.text: Strict down-up picking keeps fast lines even.
Four notes per string, down-up-down-up, across all six strings and back at 90. Keep the pick motion small.

exercises.title: Cadd9 to Dsus4
exercises.focus: Cadd9-G-Dsus4-Em at 80 bpm

sections.text: Cadd9, G and Dsus4 share the same two fingers on the top strings, so the changes ring into each other.
Anchor fingers
Keep fingers 3 and 4 on the 3rd fret of the B and high E strings for all three chords and move only the bass fingers. Then Em, with the anchors lifted.
In time
Press Play and strum along, one bar per chord. Done at three passes without a gap at the changes.

exercises.title: Bends in tune
exercises.focus: Whole-step bends in box 1 · D to E, G to A

sections.text: A bend is only good if it lands on a real note, so always check it against the note you aim for.
G string: D up to E
Play {{5}} (E, 9th fret of the G string) to hear the target. Then bend {{4}} (D, 7th fret) up a whole step with three fingers behind it until it matches. Alternate target and bend ten times.
B string: G up to A
Same on the B string: play {{1}} (A, 10th fret), then bend {{b7}} (G, 8th fret) up to it. Then bend and hold, and pick the high E's {{1}} (5th fret) against it.

exercises.title: Slow blues phrases
exercises.focus: Bends in A over drums and bass, 70 bpm

sections.text: A slow tempo leaves room for each bend to ring out; this is the scale used in blues.
One bend per phrase
Play short phrases in boxes 1 and 2, each with one bend from {{4}} to {{5}} or {{b7}} to {{1}}. Leave a bar of space between phrases.
Slide into the join
Now start each phrase with the slide from box 1 into box 2 and end it with a bend. Record a minute and listen back.

exercises.title: Legato, fingers 2-4
exercises.focus: Legato trill · fingers 2-4 · B string, 7th fret

sections.text: Fingers 2 and 4 are the weaker pair, and box 3 needs them.
Pick once, then hammer finger 4 and pull to finger 2 on the click, 30 seconds on, 15 off, three rounds at 70.

exercises.title: Chord tones over Am-F-C-G
exercises.focus: 1-3-5 of each chord · play-along in the neck view

sections.text: Playing each chord's own notes as it passes trains you to hear changes in a solo.
Slow, in the neck view
Press Play and play the notes shown, one per beat: each chord's root, 3rd, 5th, 3rd. Am has a minor 3rd ({{b3}}); F, C and G have major 3rds.
Faster, from tab
The same line at 80, reading the tab. Done at two passes without a wrong note.

exercises.title: Box 2 to box 3
exercises.focus: A minor pentatonic · boxes 2 → 3

sections.text: Box 3 carries the line up to the 13th fret, and its join is a slide on the B string.
Box 3 on its own
Box 3 up and down at 70. Find every {{1}} in it first.
Cross on the B string
Climb box 2; on the B string slide {{b7}} (G, 8th fret) up to {{1}} (A, 10th fret) and finish in box 3. Back down the same way.
Three boxes in one run
Start low in box 1, cross into box 2 on the G string, into box 3 on the B string, then all the way back. At 70; done at two clean runs.

exercises.title: Three-box solo
exercises.focus: Boxes 1-3 over Am7-Dm7, 85 bpm

sections.text: A solo that climbs through the boxes builds like a story.
Low to high
Press Play. Start in box 1 and move one box higher every four bars; land on {{a}} over Am7 and {{d}} over Dm7.
High to low
Now start in box 3 and come down a box every four bars.

exercises.title: Picking across strings
exercises.focus: Down-up, two notes per string, 100 bpm

sections.text: Two notes per string makes the pick cross strings on every upstroke, the hardest move for picking.
Two notes per string, down-up, across all six strings and back at 100. Drop to 80 if the crossings get messy.

exercises.title: Sus groove in D
exercises.focus: D-Dsus4-Dsus2 with bass-and-chord picking

sections.text: Picking the bass note and then the chord makes three shapes sound like a whole arrangement.
Bass, then chord
Press Play and copy the backing: open D string on beats 1 and 3, the top strings on 2 and 4. One bar each of D, Dsus4, D, Dsus2.
Add G and A
Now D, G, A, D with the same picking, adding a sus4 on the last beat of each bar where you can.

exercises.title: Legato in the box
exercises.focus: Hammer-ons and pull-offs in box 1 of A

sections.text: Legato inside the scale turns runs into smooth phrases.
One trill
Trill fingers 1 and 3 on the G string at the 5th fret: C to D, picking only the first note.
Through the box
Climb box 1 picking only the first note on each string and hammering the second; come down pulling off. Start and end on the low {{1}}.

exercises.title: A tune to the high Do
exercises.focus: A Ti-stage tune in D with eighth notes, up the neck

sections.text: A tune that climbs past the octave makes you shift position mid-phrase.
Learn it slowly
The tune climbs from Sol to the high Do, with a quick La-Ti-La-Sol in the middle. Press Play and follow the tab at 60, one phrase at a time.
On the neck at tempo
Now in the neck view at 80, playing it higher up so you need no open strings. Done at two clean passes.

exercises.title: Cadd9-G-Dsus4-Em, faster
exercises.focus: Anchor-finger changes at 90 bpm

sections.text: The same anchors from day 2, now as a warm-up at a faster tempo.
Press Play and strum along at 90, one bar per chord, fingers 3 and 4 never leaving the top strings until Em.

exercises.title: G minor pentatonic, boxes 1 to 3
exercises.focus: Boxes 1 → 2 → 3 in G, from the 3rd fret

sections.text: Moving the joins to a new key proves you know the shapes, not the frets.
Box 1 at the 3rd fret
G minor pentatonic box 1 starts two frets lower than A. Up and down at 70, starting on the {{1}}.
Both joins
Same joins as in A: {{4}} to {{5}} on the G string into box 2, {{b7}} to {{1}} on the B string into box 3.
At 80
Run all three boxes up and back at 80. Done at two clean runs.

exercises.title: Gm arpeggio in two boxes
exercises.focus: G minor arpeggio · boxes 1-2

sections.text: The arpeggio is the skeleton inside the scale: the notes that sound safe over Gm.
Box 1
Play {{1}} {{b3}} {{5}} up and down in box 1, one note per click at 70.
Across boxes 1 and 2
Now across both boxes, crossing at the notes they share. Then play only the {{b3}} in each box: it is the note that makes it minor.

exercises.title: Solo in G
exercises.focus: Boxes 1-3 of G minor pentatonic over Gm7-Cm7

sections.text: Aiming at the arpeggio's notes while moving through the boxes joins today's two skills.
Aim at the chord
Press Play. Land on {{g}} or {{b-flat}} over Gm7 and on {{c}} over Cm7.
Use all three boxes
Same backing; cross a join in every phrase.

exercises.title: Skip a string
exercises.focus: Down-up string skipping, 80 bpm

sections.text: Skipping a string makes the pick hand jump accurately, which wide phrases need.
Two notes per string, down-up, skipping a string each time: low E, D, B, then back. At 80; done when no wrong string sounds.

exercises.title: Em-Cadd9-G-Dsus4 in sixteenths
exercises.focus: Sixteenth strumming at 70 bpm

sections.text: Sixteenths double the hand's motion, so the groove stays tight at a slow tempo.
On Em only
Strum down-up-down-up on every beat at 70 on Em, accenting beats 2 and 4.
Over the changes
Press Play and keep the sixteenths going, one bar per chord.

exercises.title: Slide in, bend out
exercises.focus: A minor pentatonic · join 1 → 2 with a bend to finish

sections.text: A slide into box 2 followed by a bend is a classic lead move, and it uses both joins of the week.
The lick slowly
Slide {{4}} to {{5}} on the G string, play {{b7}} (G, 8th fret) on the B string, bend it up to {{1}}, release. Four beats at 60, ten times.
In box 3 too
Move it up: slide {{b7}} to {{1}} on the B string into box 3, then bend {{4}} up to {{5}} on the high E string (D at the 10th fret up to E).

exercises.title: The tune, at tempo
exercises.focus: Day 4's tune in D at 90 bpm

sections.text: Coming back to the tune two days later shows what stuck.
From memory
Play it once without the app. Then press Play and check it at 80.
Faster and with a slide
Now at 90, sliding into the high Do instead of picking it.

exercises.title: Legato check
exercises.focus: Trills 1-3 and 2-4 at 90 bpm

sections.text: The week's legato at a faster tempo, to hear the progress.
Fingers 1-3 on the G string for a minute, then fingers 2-4 on the B string for a minute, at 90. Then compare with day 1.

exercises.title: Sus part for the jam
exercises.focus: Am7-Dsus2-Dm7 rhythm part

sections.text: A sus chord between Am7 and Dm7 gives the jam a moving rhythm part.
Press Play and strum along: Am7, then Dsus2 and Dm7 two beats each. Done at four passes.

exercises.title: Three boxes from memory
exercises.focus: A minor pentatonic boxes 1-3 without the chart

sections.text: The week's key skill without help: the test that it is yours.
Without looking
Run boxes 1 to 3 and back at 80 without the chart. Then check it.
In G
Same in G, starting from the 3rd fret, still without looking.

exercises.title: The jam
exercises.focus: Boxes 1-3 with bends and slides over Am7-Dm7

sections.text: Everything from the week in one solo: joins, bends, legato and chord tones.
Chord tones first
Press Play. Land on {{a}} or {{c}} over Am7 and on {{d}} or {{f}} over Dm7.
Bends and slides
Same backing; use day 6's slide-and-bend lick at least once per chorus.
Record it
Record four minutes of soloing, climbing from box 1 to box 3 and back. Listen back and note one phrase you like for next week.
